task.title: Select the latest due recurrence through the CLI
task.objective: Complete issue https://github.com/Knosence9/project-vela/issues/915 by exposing exact latest-due recurrence selection through a thin deterministic read-only CLI adapter.
acceptance_criteria: Validate recurrence identity before storage access, open existing storage read-only, and delegate arithmetic to the kernel.
Emit compact escaped JSON preserving occurrence and continuation-cursor semantics for exact, future, and finite-completion results.
Fail with typed diagnostics, nonzero status, and empty stdout without creating missing storage or granting mutation authority.

attempts.diagnostic: The focused CLI integration test failed because latest-due was an unrecognized recurrence subcommand.
attempts.patch: Added CLI tests for bounded results, invalid and missing inputs, missing storage, and selected versus unrelated corruption before dispatch existed.

attempts.diagnostic: Added validated latest-due dispatch, read-only storage delegation, compact JSON projection, and stable typed error mapping.
attempts.patch: Implemented the command in crates/vela-dev/src/lib.rs and documented the adapter boundary in ADR-0061.

attempts.summary: Applied substantive review findings and verified the exact head.
attempts.diagnostic: CodeRabbit found that a corruption-isolation setup ignored its affected-row count and that documentation overstated one generic diagnostic. Commit 942d21d asserted a nonzero mutation and documented dedicated missing-definition and invalid-start diagnostics; both threads were resolved and the final incremental review found nothing new.
attempts.patch: Reused existing occurrence serialization, strengthened the isolation test, corrected documentation, and reran the complete quality gate on exact head 942d21d24361dd39f11c150209edc963073945d6.

outcome.summary: Operators can inspect latest-due recurrence state deterministically without the CLI reading time, writing storage, persisting a cursor, or inventing catch-up policy.

verification.command: nix develop --command cargo run --locked -p vela-dev -- record validate corpus/development/0187-latest-due-recurrence-selection-cli.json # result: valid development record
nix develop --command cargo run --locked -p vela-dev -- corpus inspect corpus/development # result: inspected 193 records: 193 valid, 0 invalid
Pull request 916 exact head 942d21d24361dd39f11c150209edc963073945d6 squash merge d3d17f08763ad53a9fe67e60401d8a1700d50bbd

lessons: A corruption-isolation test must prove that its fixture actually changed a row rather than silently accepting a stale selector.
Documentation should preserve dedicated typed exceptions instead of describing every lookup failure as one generic category.
The CLI should expose kernel projection authority without gaining persistence, scheduler-policy, or execution authority.
Validate identifiers before storage so malformed input cannot create or inspect a database.
